subject: Media Literacy
title: The Value of Personal Data
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Value of Personal Data.

hook.text: Your personal data is worth about $240 per year to advertisers. Multiply by 3 billion users and you see the economy.

buildup.text: Personal data — browsing habits, purchases, location, contacts — is the fuel of the digital advertising economy.

discovery.text: Data brokers collect and sell profiles containing thousands of data points about individuals to anyone willing to pay.

twist.text: You generate this data constantly but receive almost none of its value. The profit goes to collectors, not creators.

climax.text: Data is called 'the new oil.' Like oil, those who extract it get rich while those who produce it often don't benefit.

punchline.text: Your data is valuable. Just not to you. Not yet.

quiz.question: What are data brokers?
options: Companies that collect and sell personal profiles to anyone willing to pay
Apps that help you manage your data
